claim: TubeArchivist uses a cron-like schedule of three values (minute, hour, day-of-week), rejects number/number step syntax in the first field, and enforces a floor of no more than once per hour to avoid YouTube throttling; the Rescan Subscriptions task adds missing videos to the download queue.
quote: Cron format as number/number are non-standard cron formatting and are not supported by the scheduler... the scheduler doesn't support schedules that trigger more than once per hour.

claim: MeTube checks each subscription on a global fixed interval set by SUBSCRIPTION_DEFAULT_CHECK_INTERVAL (default 60 minutes), with SUBSCRIPTION_SCAN_PLAYLIST_END (default 50) capping newest-first entries fetched per check.
quote: SUBSCRIPTION_DEFAULT_CHECK_INTERVAL: Default minutes between automatic checks for each subscription. Defaults to 60.

claim: PinchFlat schedules the next index only after the current one completes (interval-after-completion), so a 60-minute Index Frequency plus a 30-minute index run yields a 90-minute effective cadence; Index Frequency is a per-source field and Fast Indexing (RSS by default, optional API key) speeds detection.
quote: If you set your Media Profile to index every 60 minutes and the indexing task takes 30 minutes to complete, it'll actually run every 90 minutes, since that 60 minute interval was only applied after the indexing task completed.

claim: PinchFlat's API-based fast indexing can poll roughly 65 sources at a 10-minute interval per API key, while RSS fast indexing is the no-key default sufficient for most users.
quote: by default an API key can perform fast indexing for approximately 65 sources with a polling interval of 10 minutes.

claim: ytdl-sub has no internal scheduler; the Docker image's optional cron support runs subscriptions on a user-supplied CRON_SCHEDULE (e.g. "0 */6 * * *" for every 6 hours) with no default, plus CRON_RUN_ON_START to also run at container startup.
quote: Using CRON_RUN_ON_START may cause your cron script to run too often and trigger throttles and bans... it'll run whenever the container starts, including when the host reboots, when dockerd restarts, or when a new image is pulled.

claim: TubeSync sets index frequency per-source (selectable when adding a channel/playlist), runs indexing as background scheduled tasks (Django process_tasks worker), and recommends the longest practical interval up to 24 hours to avoid endlessly re-indexing large channels.
quote: It's a good idea to add sources with as long of an index frequency as possible... it's entirely possible that your TubeSync install may spend its entire time indexing the channel, over and over again, without downloading any media.

claim: YoutubeDL-Material uses a single global check interval (subscriptions_check_interval, default 5 minutes / 300 seconds, stored in config.json) that represents the time to cycle through ALL subscriptions, so per-sub spacing = interval / number of subscriptions rather than a per-channel setting.
quote: The check interval represents the amount of time between cycling through all subscriptions. If you have 10 subscriptions and the interval is set to 100, every 10 seconds another subscription will be checked.
